limitations_and_boundaries: The study was performed in organotypic hippocampal slice cultures, which may not fully recapitulate in vivo conditions.
Elimination of postsynaptic material by microglia might occur in other brain regions, at other developmental stages, or at low frequency undetected in these experiments.
Immunofluorescent colocalization of postsynaptic proteins with microglia should be interpreted with caution due to potential non-phagocytic membrane exchange or microglial expression of PSD95.
Anecdotal electron microscopy observations of spine head filopodia converging on a microglia process require cautious extrapolation.
The mechanism of filopodia induction by microglia remains unclear.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.

methods.name: Light sheet fluorescence microscopy
methods.protocol_description: Live imaging using a Z1 light sheet microscope (Zeiss) at 35°C, 5% CO2. 60x/NA1 water-immersion objective, lateral pixel size 130 nm, axial step 480 nm. 2-color imaging: 488 and 561 nm lasers, simultaneous acquisition of GFP and tdTomato, 1 frame/45-60 s. 3-color imaging: fast switching between frames, 488/561 nm for GFP/tdTomato, 638 nm for iRFP, 1 frame/90 s. Datasets deconvolved using Zen software, drift corrected in ImageJ.
